attribution_limitations: The Figure 1 caption describes the radiolucent lesion as spanning the whole length of the mandible "from one condyle to the other", while the case text states the lesion spared both condyles. The caption wording may only mean the lesion spans the mandible between the condyles; the source does not resolve it.

The discussion reports no Ki-67 and bcl-2 reduction at "the above site" where the lesion did not resolve with marsupialization alone, but the sentence does not name the site, and the case paragraph describes immunohistochemistry only for the pretreatment biopsy (lower anterior and lower left tissues) and for the base of the resolved lesion.

The abstract states complete resolution at 40 months and that the case was followed for 10 years, but the anchor of the 40 months is not stated (surgery versus marsupialization). Separately, the case text reports the 42 and 43 curettage after 2 years and a further 6-month non-resolution, with no wording of recurrence.

Figure callouts in the text do not match the printed caption numbers: the text cites Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 for histology (captions Figure 4 and Figure 5), Fig. 4 after 2 years (caption Figure 2 is a 2-year radiograph) and Fig. 5 for 10 years (caption Figure 3). The image assets agree with their own captions (Figures 1 to 3 are panoramic radiographs, Figures 4 and 5 are histology), so the mismatch lies in the in-text callouts; attribution follows the captions.

Dental region labels differ between sentences (mandibular right quadrant / 4th quadrant at 4 months; 42 and 43 region at 2 years; region between lower right lateral incisor and canine in the Figure 2 caption; lower right anterior region in the abstract). The source does not state they are the same region.

The abstract states the case was followed for 10 years with no sign of relapse and reoccurrence, while the image-only Table 1 (pixel content, recorded in visual.json only) prints a row labelled as an observed recurrence during that follow-up period. The text itself describes the 2-year finding as persistent radiolucency and incomplete resolution, not as recurrence.
